_comment: Feature 135 app-facing AI client contract for 3.13.101. Accepted in ADR-0053 on 2026-08-14. All ten invariant groups are proven by four real-socket suites and 40 targeted mutation checks. The deterministic collaborator is a real local HTTP server reached over a real socket, never a client mock.

invariants.rule: Ai exposes chat, complete, and embed in every framework. Vision, image, ask, ask_json, agents, tools, and conversation state are not aliases or hidden second surfaces in 3.13.101.
invariants.why: One small portable API is the feature. Shipping both the audited Ai contract and the older unimplemented Llm proposal would create divergence before the first release.

invariants.rule: OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic non-streaming chat responses normalize to text, model, usage(prompt/completion/total tokens), finish reason, and raw provider response; missing required content raises AiParseError.
invariants.why: Application code must not contain provider-specific field traversal or mistake malformed success payloads for valid empty replies.

invariants.rule: complete(prompt) sends exactly one user message through chat and returns only normalized response text.
invariants.why: The convenience method must be a thin route through the proven chat path, not a second transport implementation.

invariants.rule: embed(string) returns one numeric vector and embed(list of strings) returns one numeric vector per input in input order; malformed or missing vectors raise AiParseError.
invariants.why: A caller can use embeddings immediately without provider-shape conversion or guessing which input a vector belongs to.

invariants.rule: Ai.chat(stream=true) yields a typed AiEvent iterator. The union is {type:'text_delta'|'tool_call'|'done'|'error', ...}. Text deltas arrive per chunk; tool_calls are aggregated (buffered until args JSON parses and emitted as one event with id+name+args); done fires exactly once after all deltas; error fires only for mid-stream failures and replaces done. Ordering matches wire order. No retry after the first event.
invariants.why: An agent loop cannot see tool_calls or finish_reason under the string-only shape from ADR-0053. Typed events let the caller pattern-match without hand-rolled SSE parsing per app.

invariants.rule: message.content accepts a string OR a list of parts {type:'text', text} | {type:'image', source} where source is a data:<media_type>;base64,<payload> URI or an https:// URL. Providers get their native shape (OpenAI/local: image_url; Anthropic: content-block with base64|url). Malformed parts raise AiConfigError before any request is sent.
invariants.why: Multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude vision, local llava) all accept image parts. String-only content locks out this whole class of use.

invariants.rule: Every configurable call option resolves explicit argument over TINA4_AI_* environment over documented default, identically in all four frameworks.
invariants.why: The engineer must be able to override one request without rewriting process configuration, and the same deployment variables must behave everywhere.

invariants.rule: OpenAI and Anthropic send no request when TINA4_AI_KEY is absent. The key, prompt, and response body never appear in logs, inspection, or error text. Local works without a key.
invariants.why: A secret must not leak through the developer surfaces this framework provides, and a missing hosted credential is configuration failure rather than an anonymous network request.

invariants.rule: Retries are bounded by TINA4_AI_MAX_RETRIES and occur only before output for connection failures, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx. Retry-After is honoured within the total deadline. Other 4xx and parse failures are attempted once.
invariants.why: Bounded transient recovery adds resilience without hiding permanent failures or duplicating streamed output.

invariants.rule: TINA4_AI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT bounds connection establishment and TINA4_AI_TIMEOUT bounds the whole request including retries and body/stream reads; both paths raise AiTimeoutError without an unbounded hang.
invariants.why: One overloaded socket timeout cannot promise an end-to-end deadline, especially across retries and streaming reads.

invariants.rule: The client uses only each language standard library and its deterministic contract suite reaches a real local HTTP server over a real socket; no provider SDK or mocked client collaborator is used.
invariants.why: The feature must preserve Tina4's zero-dependency promise while proving the real transport, headers, body, deadlines, and streaming parser.
